rv.q: I can't remember when I saw a play that was so utterly clear yet had such a startling destination.
Strange, silly and savage, then – and I'd say borderline unmissable.
There’s a frazzled lunacy to David Ireland ‘s black comedy.
By the end of the evening, it becomes the kind of shocker that would definitely be X-rated if shown in a cinema.
There is no doubt that it is an extraordinary achievement, and certainly the most powerful piece of new writing on the London stage.

cn.t: Ireland's darkly comic satire on Northern Irish sectarianism shocks and provokes with its blend of horror and humor. Critics praise Rea's performance and the production's clarity, though the disturbing material leaves audiences unsettled.
